newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says anti-Helms-Burton, not pro-Castro.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says anti-Helms-Burton, not pro-Castro.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said Tuesday he told Cuba he opposed U.S. plans to tighten the trade embargo on Havana, but that that should not be read as as sign of support for President Fidel Castro.
"We may not share the proposal ... contained in the Helms-Burton law, but neither do we share (the principles) of the Cuban regime," he told foreign correspondents.

Menem said he made that point clear to Cuban Deputy President Carlos Lage, who last week visited Argentina as part of an 18-nation tour by Cuban officials seeking help against U.S. Congress moves to tighten the 35-year-old embargo.

The Argentine leader, a staunch opponent of the Castro regime, said, "I am dead set against tyrannies and dictactorships and in favor of democracy. And in Cuba there is no democracy, neither are human rights respected."
